lesson.text: Quick memory: what is one thing to keep private online? (Your address, your school, your password…) Today: being kind online.
Behind every name in a game is a real person with real feelings. Be as kind online as you would be face to face.
Before you send a message, stop and think: is it true? Is it kind? Would I say it to their face?
Being mean to someone online, again and again on purpose, is called cyberbullying. It is never OK, and it is never the fault of the person it happens to.
If something online upsets or worries you: stop, don't reply, and tell a grown-up you trust. You won't be in trouble for telling.
In this game you can MUTE someone, BLOCK them, or REPORT them (MEAN WORDS, SCARY, ASKED SECRETS). A real person reads every report.
Be an upstander: if you see someone being unkind to another player, don't join in. Send a kind message to the one who was hurt, and tell a grown-up.

picture.name: Zara
messages: I liked your castle. Build together?

lesson.text: Try it in the world: build a kindness corner in your world with a bench and flowers. When a friend visits, say one kind thing about what they built.

exercises.prompt: The people you meet in online games have real feelings.
exercises.hint: Who is behind each player's name?
exercises.explain: True: behind every name is a real person with real feelings.

exercises.prompt: Sort these messages: kind or unkind?
exercises.hint: How would you feel if someone sent it to you?
exercises.explain: Kind: Good job!, Thanks for helping!, Let's build together! The others would hurt someone's feelings.

exercises.prompt: Something online makes you feel upset. What should you do first?
choices: stop, and tell a grown-up you trust
keep playing and hope it stops
exercises.explain: Stop, don't reply, and tell a grown-up you trust. You won't be in trouble.

exercises.prompt: Which is a kind thing to say to a new player?
exercises.hint: Which words would make you feel welcome?
choices: Hi! Want to build with us?
exercises.explain: “Hi! Want to build with us?” makes a new player feel welcome.

choices: being mean online again and again, on purpose
exercises.explain: Cyberbullying is being mean to someone online, again and again, on purpose.

exercises.prompt: Match each button in the game to what it does.
exercises.hint: Remember the lesson card about the three buttons.
exercises.explain: MUTE: no invites from them. BLOCK: they are not your friend anymore. REPORT: a person checks what happened.

exercises.prompt: If someone is mean to you online, it is your fault.
exercises.explain: False: it is never the fault of the person it happens to. Tell a grown-up you trust.

exercises.prompt: Before you send a message, what should you ask yourself?
exercises.hint: Remember: true, kind, and would I say it to their face?
exercises.explain: Ask: is it true? Is it kind? Would I say it to their face?

exercises.prompt: Zara's friend is being teased in the chat. What could Zara do?
exercises.hint: Be an upstander, not a bystander.
choices: send a kind message and tell a grown-up
exercises.explain: Zara can send her friend a kind message and tell a grown-up. That is being an upstander.

exercises.prompt: Something scary pops up in a game. Put what to do in order.
exercises.hint: First keep yourself safe, then get help.
items: Close it or leave the game
exercises.explain: Stop and don't reply, close it or leave the game, then tell a grown-up you trust.

exercises.hint: They stand up for someone else.
choices: someone who helps when they see unkindness
someone who stands up in class
someone who joins in the teasing
exercises.explain: An upstander helps when they see someone being unkind to another person.

exercises.prompt: You will be in trouble if you tell a grown-up about something bad you saw online.
exercises.hint: What do grown-ups want to know?
exercises.explain: False: telling a grown-up is always the right thing, and you won't be in trouble for it.

exercises.prompt: Bram sent a message in a rush, and now he thinks it was unkind. What is the best thing to do?
exercises.hint: What would you want if someone was unkind to you?
exercises.explain: Saying sorry helps put it right, and next time he can stop and think before he sends.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: kind to do online, or never do?
items: leave a player out on purpose
exercises.hint: Would it make the other player feel good or bad?
exercises.explain: Kind: say good game, help a new player, say thanks. Never: share secrets, make fun, leave someone out.

exercises.prompt: Which message would you be happy to say to someone's face?
choices: Nice castle! How did you make the tower?
exercises.explain: “Nice castle! How did you make the tower?” is kind and friendly.

exercises.prompt: Cyberbullying is unkind again and again, on purpose. Sort them: cyberbullying, or a one-off mistake?
items: mean messages every day, on purpose
a rude word by mistake, then sorry
leaving one player out of every game
a friend forgot to invite you once
exercises.hint: Ask two questions: does it happen again and again? Is it on purpose?
exercises.explain: Cyberbullying: daily mean messages and leaving someone out every time happen again and again, on purpose. A one-off mistake: the rude word was an accident and they said sorry; forgetting once was not on purpose.
